$comment: One checklist check row — the machine form of a v5 checklist Sheet line. It ships as an example
because until 28/07/2026 this was the ONLY schema in the kit with no example at all, which meant
kit-lint L8 (every shipped example validates against its schema) exercised the shape zero times.
The row is deliberately an AWKWARD one rather than a clean pass, because the clean case teaches
nothing: it shows one platform Failed and another Skipped in the same round, which is where the
status vocabulary is easiest to get wrong.
`statuses` is ONE ENTRY PER PLATFORM SUB-COLUMN, in block order (here: iOS, Android). The Sheet
dropdown knows exactly four values and no others:
'Passed'  — something objective said so; name it in the oracle.
'Failed'  — a real defect; the comment carries the BUG-NNN link.
'Skipped' — will NOT be run on this platform (feature absent, screen unreachable, blocked and
not going to unblock). A DECISION, so a reason is mandatory.
''        — not run YET this round. Temporary, and still requires a comment saying why.
'Partial' is a real and visible value of a checklist row — just not of THIS field. It belongs to
the row's computed RESULT column (amber), which the Sheet derives per block: Failed short-circuits,
then Partial when some active platform is still empty, then Passed / Skipped / ''. That column's
vocabulary is free precisely because nobody types into it. So: writing 'Partial' into `statuses`
is what fabricates a verdict — a human declaring the summary instead of letting it be derived.
And that is why this schema carries no `result` field at all. The result is DERIVABLE from
`statuses` plus which platforms are active this round, and a derived value stored beside its
inputs is a value that will eventually disagree with them — the same reason the RTM is a
projection and a test report's counts are computed rather than typed. If you need the result in
a machine form, recompute it; do not persist it here.
`check` should imply its own oracle ('matches Figma node X', 'matches the spec'), so a reader can
tell what would decide it before running anything — a check nobody can decide is not a check.
check: Wrong password shows the inline error under the field and keeps the entered email
comment: iOS: the error appears at the top of the screen instead of under the field and the email is cleared — BUG-014. Android: skipped this round — the build ships with the new sign-in behind a feature flag that is off on staging, so the screen is unreachable rather than broken.

oracle.source: sign-in error-state design + the acceptance criterion 'entered email is preserved'
